newsitem.title: CHINA: China Q1 consumer price inflation 5.2 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: China Q1 consumer price inflation 5.2 pct - paper.

text.p: China's first quarter consumer price inflation was 5.2 percent, the official Economic Daily said on Friday.
The rate in March alone stood at 4 percent, the paper said.
Consumer price inflation for February was 5.6 percent year on year.
China previously reported its benchmark retail price inflation rose a meagre 1.7 percent in March and 2.6 percent in the first quarter.
The newspaper, quoting the State Statistical Bureau, also said that both measures of inflation showed the lowest increases for any first quarter since 1992.
Abundant supplies of food had kept food price rises at modest levels, the newspaper said. It added that the state has been carefully monitoring the price situation to keep price rises under control.
China has forecast benchmark retail price inflation for the whole year at 6.0 percent compared with 6.1 percent last year and 14.8 percent in 1995.
